historical_references.reference: Evarista of Córdoba was a Spanish Christian martyr who lived during the Moorish occupation of Spain (8th century). She was a maidservant who refused to renounce her faith, and was tortured and executed. Her cultus developed in the 15th century and she became the patroness of domestic servants.

Saint Evaristus was a pope and a martyr who ruled from 95 to 100 A.D. He was a Roman by birth, and was deeply revered for his learning and holiness. He was a victim of the persecutions of Emperor Trajan, and was buried on the Via Appia in Rome. His cultus developed rapidly after his death and he became associated with the miraculous multiplication of the loaves and fishes.
